Why go: room for a family or group, without paying for 15

Siriwan's base price covers up to 8 guests, so a group of 6–8 doesn't pay extra to have a twin-engine speedboat to themselves. Twin engines mean a steadier, safer ride on the longer runs to Ang Thong and Koh Tao. Every route is a full day of about 8.5 hours, with a captain, a deckhand and a guide.

Koh Tan and Pig Island is the short, calm option. Add Koh Rap for a quiet beach and fewer boats. Koh Phangan suits snorkelling and long lunches. Ang Thong (from 16 December) brings the Emerald Lake on Koh Mae Ko and the viewpoints. The Koh Tao route starts at Koh Nang Yuan, three islets joined by a sandbar, and then snorkels Koh Tao's bays, where the water is often clearest.

Who it suits, and who should choose something else

  • Good for: families and friends travelling as 5–8, multi-generation groups and anyone heading to Koh Tao who wants twin-engine reliability.
  • Choose something else if: you're only 2–4 people. The Little Voyager or Wally cost less. For a shared Koh Tao day at a per-person price, see our Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan trip.

Good to know

  • Koh Nang Yuan rules: the island charges a landing fee and doesn't allow plastic bottles. Bring a refillable bottle.
  • Sea by month: February to September is best for Koh Tao and Ang Thong. In the north-east monsoon (October to December), the southern islands are the safest bet.
  • Transfer: one van covers the whole group both ways, so it costs little per head.
  • Lunch: restaurants on Koh Tao and Koh Phangan beaches are mostly cash only. Bring enough for the whole group.
